newsitem.title: ITALY: Auditors see risks in Italy's mini Gemina.
newsitem.headline: Auditors see risks in Italy's mini Gemina.

text.p: Auditors for financial holding group Gemina fear that a move to hive off its industrial interests into a new company could raise the risk linked to its troubled Gemina Capital Markets unit.
The auditors issued the warning in a document relating to the split of Gemina's industrial holdings into Holding di Partecipazioni Industriali (HPI) announced earlier this month.

They said that, even if the potential risk remained around an estimated 70 billion lire, the ratio between "risk funds" and "economic value" -- now at 1.77 percent -- would rise to 24.91 percent for the far less capitalised "mini" Gemina.

Today's Gemina has charges on a book value of 2.32 trillion lire -- which could be raised to 3.95 trillion by official evaluators -- but the same charge will weigh on the "mini" Gemina, whose book value will be only 248 billion lire, or 281 billion if revalued.
The bulk of Gemina's assets will be transferred to HPI, which will have an estimated book value of 2.07 trillion lire.
Gemina has said a stock market listing would be sought for the new HPI company, but has not said when the split will take place.
The internal auditors called for a complete outlining of the evaluation criteria for all risks and assets at Gemina's next shareholders meeting at the end of November.
Gemina shares closed 1.99 percent down at 683.6 lire on Wednesday on an easier Milan stock exchange.
